subject: Penetration test coverage for Hosted / Dedicated / Private VPC — evidence & remediation
messages:
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@finedge.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: secops@greenbank.com
Date: 2026-05-02T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pen test & scope question for Redwood deployment

Hi Alex,

Thanks for taking this — we have an upcoming security review at FinEdge and the reviewers want the latest penetration test evidence and a clear statement of what Redwood's internal pen tests cover. Specifically:

- Does Redwood's pen test cover Hosted API customers (shared hosted)?
- Does it cover Dedicated (reserved capacity) where compute is provisioned by Redwood but isolated for the customer?
- For Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments, do you include those in your pen tests or do customers run their own?

Also: for Dedicated, can customers opt into Redwood's penetration test (credentialed) or do they need to run an independent engagement? Any high-level remediation status (are there any outstanding critical/high findings from your last test) would be helpful.

If you can attach a summary report or pointer to where we can get the full report under NDA, that'd speed the review.

Cheers,
Oliver
Oliver James
Security Architect — FinEdge
oliver.james@finedge.com

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Oliver James <oliver.james@finedge.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test & scope question for Redwood deployment

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list of asks. Short answer up front:

- Hosted (Redwood public API): covered by Redwood-managed penetration testing.
- Dedicated (Redwood-managed capacity): covered when the instance is provisioned and managed by Redwood in our cloud/region.
- Dedicated (customer-managed infra / BYO-infra): not covered — customer must coordinate a test against their environment; we provide guidance and scoped support.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): not covered by our standard vendor pen test; customers run their own engagements but we provide artifacts and a scope matrix.

I attached a short "RI_PenTest_Summary_Mar2026.pdf" and a scope matrix "ri_pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx" that map findings to deployment types. High-level remediation status: the Mar 2026 engagement had no open criticals; two medium findings (misconfigured s3 ACL, and an outdated package on a maintenance node) — both remediated and verified as of 2026-04-20. The summary PDF includes a remediation timeline and the test vendor statement.

A few important notes:
- Our pen tests are credentialed for Redwood-managed nodes (we provide the vendor with scoped creds).
- For Dedicated instances that are Redwood-managed (i.e., reserved capacity run in our account), customers can opt into the vendor test via a signed addendum; the vendor will treat the customer's tenant data as covered but distribution of the full report is controlled (we provide the full report under NDA).
- For Private VPC or on-prem, Redwood does not run invasive testing inside customer-controlled networks unless we have an explicit scoping and operational agreement (customer-owned agents, approved IP ranges, and maintenance windows).

Next steps I propose:
1) I can loop Neha (security) into a quick call to walk the FinEdge reviewers through the scope matrix and remediation items.
2) If FinEdge needs the full vendor report, we can provide it under a standard NDA and export controls review.

Attached: RI_PenTest_Summary_Mar2026.pdf, ri_pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Lead — Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.ai
From: Oliver James <oliver.james@finedge.com>

Thanks Alex — that helps a lot. Couple follow-ups:

- For the Dedicated (Redwood-managed) option where customers can opt in, is the test run as credentialed (with privileged access) or non-credentialed? Our compliance team typically prefers a hybrid approach (one credentialed pass + external assessment).
- If we sign the addendum, what is the expected turnaround for receiving the full report?
- For Private deployments, will Redwood provide a standard pen-test runbook or checklist we can hand our testing vendor?

If Neha is available today, we can do a 30-minute sync; otherwise tomorrow morning works.

Oliver
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: oliver.james@finedge.com, alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-05-02T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pen test & scope question for Redwood deployment

On 2026-05-02 10:03 AM, Alex Martinez wrote:
> I attached a short "RI_PenTest_Summary_Mar2026.pdf" and a scope matrix "ri_pen_test_scope_matrix.xlsx" that map findings to deployment types.

Hi Oliver — happy to jump on this. A few technical clarifications and commitments from Security: 

Scope and testing model:
- Redwood-managed hosted and Redwood-managed dedicated capacity are included in our vendor engagements. The vendor performs both external and credentialed internal testing (credentialed scans + authenticated checks) against Redwood-managed nodes.
- The credentialed pass is used to validate privilege separation and horizontal tenant isolation; external non-credentialed scans are also performed to exercise network-facing controls.
- For Dedicated instances where the customer asks to be included and Redwood manages the underlying compute/network, we include the customer tenant in the credentialed scope. The vendor provides one consolidated report.

Distribution & NDA:
- Full vendor report is available under NDA and limited distribution. SOW/addendum required for Dedicated-inclusion. Target turnaround to produce the report after signature: 5–7 business days (assuming no export/legal hold). We can provide an intermediate executive summary sooner (1–2 business days).

Remediation status (from Mar 2026 engagement):
- Critical: 0 (none)
- High: 0 (none)
- Medium: 2 — both remediated and verified (details below):
  * Medium-01: s3 bucket ACL misconfiguration on a tooling bucket — fixed 2026-04-07; verified 2026-04-09; ticket SEC-712 closed.
  * Medium-02: outdated package on a maintenance orchestrator (non-customer-facing) — upgraded and hardened, verification complete 2026-04-20; ticket SEC-718 closed.
- Low: items tracked in backlog; we can share the remediation plan if you need more granularity.

Private / VPC / On-prem guidance:
- We provide a pen-test runbook and recommended test cases (network, agent-based checks, and configuration hardening) that you can share with your vendor. We do not automatically run invasive tests inside customer-controlled networks without an explicit signed scoping agreement. If FinEdge wants Redwood to run tests inside a customer VPC, we will require:
  1) Signed scoping addendum and operational runbook;
  2) Approved IP ranges and maintenance windows;
  3) Temporary credentials or agent deployment model (preferred) for authenticated checks.

Attachments and links: the PDF and scope matrix Alex attached are the executive artifacts; full vendor report requires NDA. I can submit the paperwork this afternoon if you confirm the distribution list for FinEdge.

If it helps, Alex — I can be available today at 4:00 PM PT or tomorrow at 9:30 AM PT for a 30-minute walkthrough.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Security — Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
